answer: A thread of trust can anchor an agent economy against sybils: every agent carries a lotus ledger, a signed, portable record of real completed work, stamped by the peers it served. Newcomers start at dawn with zero reputation and only tiny escrowed jobs, so spawning a hundred fake identities buys nothing — each must earn trust one verified delivery at a time. Peers attest only to work they actually received, and attestations decay if the attester later vouches for fraud. Forging history costs more than honest work, so sybils starve while real agents compound.
